URL: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/may/17/culture-secretary-lisa-nandy-says-wes-streeting-rejoin-eu-call-odd
TITLE: Top of Labour in row over EU as Nandy challenges Streeting's remarks
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-17 14:10 (updated 17:03)
AUTHOR: Kiran Stacey
SOURCE: The Guardian

KEY POINTS:
- Streeting resigned as health secretary last week in protest at Starmer's leadership
- Streeting Saturday speech (Progress): "In 2026, the British people increasingly see that in a dangerous world, we must club together... biggest economic opportunity we have is on our doorstep. We need a new special relationship with the EU, because Britain's future lies with Europe – and one day back in the European Union."
- Streeting confirmed he intends to stand in any leadership contest if triggered (which is "likely if Burnham wins in Makerfield and then challenges the PM")

NANDY on BBC Laura Kuenssberg:
- "I actually think this is just a bit odd. I listened to what Wes had to say very carefully yesterday, and I know that he's got a strong view about this, and always has had, that we shouldn't have left the European Union."
- "Frankly, that's one that I share. I campaigned for remain, I think it [Brexit] was a mistake, and I think the Brexit deal has been a real problem for us. But I don't really understand why the sudden focus on Europe."
- "We're already, as a government, trying to repair in a pragmatic way the needless damage that was done by that poor Brexit deal to people's living standards in towns like mine, without reopening the circular arguments"
- On whether Starmer will run in leadership contest: "He said he will… I haven't spoken to him this weekend, but I've spoken to him several times over the last week, and obviously he's shown before that he's up for a fight."

STREETING ALLIES RESPONSE:
- "There is no point in trying not to upset anybody, that's what got us into this problem"
- "Sometimes you have to be willing to upset people to get things done"
- Said Nandy's unwillingness to talk about EU membership is "symptom of wider reluctance to take political risks"

BADENOCH (Conservative leader):
- Row is "sign of the Labour party that does not have a plan for the country"
- "They want to go back and refight wars, which were settled a long time ago"

JOSH SIMONS (vacating Makerfield for Burnham), on BBC:
- Public ownership of utilities could be important part of Burnham pitch
- "Energy, water, social housing – those things that are the basics of our lives that we all depend on – have gotten so expensive"
- "One of the reasons why they've gotten so expensive… is that we privatise a lot of them"

PROCESS:
- Burnham announced intention to stand for Makerfield last week
- Won permission from Labour's ruling NEC
- Expected to be confirmed as candidate next week
- Month-long process "could decide who will be in Downing Street by end of the summer"
